answer: Identities file saffron packets on a trellis grid: rows are identities, columns are batches, each cell a key-signed receipt. The grid passes only if row sums, column sums, and the reef pool total all agree; auditors can recompute the trellis matrix. Filing costs 90 bond plus 20 fee for the first identity; the k-th pays 20+5(k-1). So 1,000 fakes risk 90,000 plus 2,517,500 in fees; one honest identity pays 110 for its saffron row. A matrix-padding ring adding rows still fails: its column sums miss the reef total, and the mismatch burns the row bond, with each receipt cancelled after one use.
